.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1134 PM CDT Sun Sep 27 2026

A wet pattern is expected this week, with periods of showers and 
thunderstorms and a risk of locally heavy rainfall through the 
upcoming weekend.

Hot weather continues today with a gradual increase in humidity 
throughout the day. Although the mid to upper level ridge continues 
to weaken and move out of the region, sufficient subsidence remains 
to inhibit widespread convection today. However, isolated, diurnally 
driven showers/storms remain possible. Rain and storm chances 
increase slightly Tuesday as weak vorticity maxima aloft move over 
the region. WIll continue with 15% to 25% chance, mainly for the 
afternoon. 

We will continue to monitor the next rainmaker system. A slow-moving 
mid to upper level longwave trough will continue to move over the 
western CONUS today, merging with the remnants of what is now 
Hurricane Polo near Baja California late tonight into Tuesday. 
Deep Pacific and tropical moisture will be enhanced at the mid to 
upper levels as the trough moves over the southern Rockies/West 
Texas. Additionally, a strong southerly influx of humid Gulf 
airmass will filter across the region, resulting in PWATs in the 
2.0 - 2.4 inch range across Southeast Texas through the weekend. 
These values are in the 90th to 97th percentile of climatology per
NAEFS, GEFS and ENS. In terms of standard deviation, these PWAT 
values are 2 sigma above normal (2-3 near the Brazos Valley), 
suggesting heavy rainfall that could result in localized flooding.
Therefore, showers and thunderstorms will continue to increase on
Wednesday, particularly during peak daytime heating due to the 
combination of deep moisture and mesoscale boundaries such as 
seabreezes or outflow boundaries from convection developing across
central TX. 

PWs peak on Thursday and Friday as the main trough digs across the 
Plains/north-central TX. Global guidance shows a general consensus 
on timing, but there are still discrepancies regarding the evolution 
of the system once it approaches our region. Most models suggest a 
swath of heavy rainfall extending across central Texas, potentially 
reaching our western counties by Thursday. Confidence in the final 
location of this axis of convergence and heavy rain is low to 
moderate. So, it will need to be monitored closely in the coming 
days, especially for our western zones, including the Brazos Valley. 
While the general consensus at the moment brings the heaviest band 
of precipitation west of I-45, we will continue to monitor impacts 
for higher totals east of I-45 and across the coastal zones through 
the weekend as PWs remain elevated. Specific details on rainfall 
amounts remain uncertain. Will continue to monitor trends for any 
upward or downward adjustments in the coming days. In the meantime, 
remain weather aware and keep in mind that periods of showers and 
storms are expected, mainly from Wednesday into the weekend with a 
risk of heavy rainfall leading to localized flooding. 

This system will drag a weak cold front through sometime late Friday 
or Saturday with rain chances gradually diminishing through the 
weekend. While the front itself won't have a significant impact on 
temperatures, precipitation chances and increased cloud cover will 
keep temperatures near seasonal levels through most of the forecast 
period.  

JM

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAF Issuance)
Issued at 629 AM CDT Mon Sep 28 2026

Continued VFR conditions today and tonight for most terminals.
Light winds this morning become SE and increase to 8-13kt later
this afternoon. Could see some brief, higher-end MVFR fog during 
the late night and early morning hours west of I-45. 47 

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1134 PM CDT Sun Sep 27 2026

Light onshore winds and low seas will persist through at least 
Tuesday along with isolated showers and storms. Rain and storm 
chances will increase after Tuesday as a disturbance moves over the 
Plains and pushes a frontal boundary off the coast sometime upcoming 
weekend. Therefore, a daily risk of showers and storms can be 
expected during the second half of the week, peaking Thursday and 
Friday. Elevated winds and building seas (up to 7-8ft) are also 
anticipated. A Small Craft Advisory will likely be needed late 
Tuesday or Wednesday. 

JM
